name: Non-Blockingness Verification Benchmarks for Bounded Petri Nets
description: In this paper, we study the problem of non-blockingness verification by tapping into the basis reachability graph (BRG). Non-blockingness is a property that ensures that all pre-specified tasks can be completed, which is a mandatory requirement during the system design stage. In this paper we develop a condition of transition partition of a given net such that the corresponding conflict-increase BRG contains sufficient information on verifying non-blockingness of its corresponding Petri net. Thanks to the compactness of the BRG, our approach possesses practical efficiency since the exhaustive enumeration of the state space can be avoided. In particular, our method does not require that the net is deadlock-free.
reputation: Niche academic benchmark used within formal methods and Petri-net verification research with limited broad community adoption.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on Petri-net properties; evaluations commonly report correctness plus runtime/memory; dataset sizes and modeling choices can strongly affect results.
